title: [Task Sprint] QA Testing Report — Panorra API New

issues.main_description_html:
QA Summary - 6 August 2026

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED. Developer comments and the active-tour API update were reviewed. The TourMkr active-tour integration itself returned a valid real response, but the shared RabbitMQ package contains unresolved Git merge-conflict markers. The cronjob package therefore cannot compile, blocking the notification worker from opening a queue channel, sending the notification email, or updating the affected post. No state-changing cronjob call was made because it could process real owners' records.

Scope and safety

Item Result
Environment Dev Panorra API and live GoThru active-tour API
Developer updates reviewed Worker email implementation; active-tour endpoint changed to /panorra/check-active-tour?tour_key=
Persistent mutation None; invoking the notification cronjob can send email, set pending=true, and clear queued embed records
HTTP 500 Not observed

Real API test results

ID Scenario Endpoint Expected Actual Result
API-01 Dev dependency health GET /check-connection Dependencies available for integration 200; database, Redis, RabbitMQ, SMTP, and Elasticsearch reported up PASS
API-02 Active TourMkr check, F1 tour key GET https://apil.gothru.co/panorra/check-active-tour?tour_key=gvbw5zEr Controlled activity response 200, fov=true, gov=false PASS
CR-01 Compile notification dependency src/Utils/RabbitMQ/RabbitMQ.go Valid Go source Go parser failed on unresolved merge markers FAIL: coding bug

Confirmed coding bug

Bug Evidence User impact Required correction
Unresolved merge conflicts in shared RabbitMQ implementation Literal <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> exist at lines 18-22, 28-48, and 65-83; parser reports expected 'IDENT', found '<<' Notification TourMkr cannot build; it cannot open a RabbitMQ channel, queue email_tourmkr, or complete its post-state integration Resolve all conflict blocks, keep one connection lifecycle implementation and the required publish helper, then run formatting/build and a fixture-scoped cronjob test

Copyable, sanitized requests and responses

GET https://apil.gothru.co/panorra/check-active-tour?tour_key=gvbw5zEr
{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "messages": "Data retrieved",
    "fov": true,
    "gov": false
  }
}

The job extracts F1 or G1 from a TourMkr embed identifier, sends the remaining key to the active-tour endpoint, and determines whether notification is needed from fov or gov. Tester identity, embed slug, recipient, and queue payload are intentionally redacted.

Test-design coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Dependency health and real active-tour contract PASS
Gray-box Checked F1/G1 key parsing and activity-flag decision path against the live service contract Active-tour integration matched the expected response shape
White-box Reviewed cronjob selection, status decision, email-queue publication, post pending update, and shared RabbitMQ implementation FAIL: shared dependency cannot compile
Confusion matrix Not applicable: this deterministic integration is not a classifier N/A

Code review

Area Finding Assessment
Route GET /cronjob/notification-tourmkr is registered Present
Active-tour integration Uses the developer-specified check-active-tour endpoint Real response validated
Decision rule F1 uses fov; G1 uses gov; inactive/error result becomes notification candidate Present in source
Notification and state Candidate messages use email_tourmkr, then set the related post pending=true Blocked by RabbitMQ compilation failure
Queue maintenance Replaces the queued TourMkr embed list after processing Not run to avoid affecting unknown owners

Conclusion

This is a developer-facing coding bug: unresolved merge conflicts in the shared RabbitMQ package block the TourMkr notification integration. The active-tour API itself responded correctly. Re-test the actual cronjob only after the conflict is resolved and a tester-owned TourMkr embed fixture is confirmed, because the successful path can send email and change post state.

QA Summary - 6 August 2026

Verdict: PASSED. The authenticated OTP Delete Account request successfully generated and sent a deletion-verification OTP to the approved Dev tester inbox. The destructive deactivate endpoint was deliberately not called, so the tester account remains active and no deletion request was created. No HTTP 500 or coding bug was observed.

Scope and safety

Item Result
Environment Dev: https://app2-dev.panorra.com
Developer update reviewed Implement Worker Send Email
Approved test account Dev tester account; identity, token, and OTP value redacted
Persistent mutation One short-lived Delete Account OTP was created or refreshed and delivered to the approved tester inbox
Explicitly not run POST /users/deactivate; this endpoint would deactivate the account and create a deletion request
Account status Remains active; no deletion/deactivation request submitted

Real API test results

ID Scenario Endpoint Expected Actual Result
API-01 Unauthenticated control POST /users/otp-delete without token Reject anonymous caller 401 Unauthorized PASS
API-02 Authenticate approved Dev tester POST /auth Valid user session 200 Login success PASS
API-03 Generate deletion OTP POST /users/otp-delete with user token Create/refresh OTP and queue delivery email 200 OTP Has ben sent to your E-Mail PASS
API-04 Deactivate account POST /users/deactivate Would consume OTP and deactivate account Not run by design NOT APPLICABLE

Copyable, sanitized request and response

POST https://app2-dev.panorra.com/users/otp-delete
Authorization: {redacted-dev-tester-token}
role: user
stage: dev
Accept: application/json
{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "OTP Has ben sent to your E-Mail"
  }
}

No request body is required. Do not expose the authorization token, recipient address, or OTP value.

Test-design coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Anonymous rejection, authenticated OTP generation, and email-delivery trigger PASS
Gray-box Verified the authenticated branch that checks for an existing delete request, creates/refreshes a 15-minute OTP, and publishes an email message PASS
White-box Reviewed authentication, existing-request guard, OTP upsert, email queue publication, and separate deactivate endpoint PASS for OTP scope
Confusion matrix Not applicable: deterministic authorization and OTP workflow, not a classifier N/A

Code review

Area Finding Assessment
Route POST /users/otp-delete is registered Present
Authorization Uses authenticated user context and rejects missing token Runtime 401 confirmed
Duplicate guard Rejects callers with an existing deletion request Present in source
OTP lifecycle Creates or refreshes a Delete Account OTP with 15-minute expiration Authenticated runtime trigger succeeded
Email hand-off Queues email_delete_account after OTP persistence Runtime endpoint returned success; sensitive OTP excluded
Account safety Account deactivation is a separate POST /users/deactivate action Not called; tester account remains active

Conclusion

The OTP Delete Account API passed within the safe approved scope. It correctly rejects unauthenticated access and successfully triggers a deletion-verification OTP for an authorized tester without deactivating the account. No coding bug is reported.

• Encrypt cry data - [ ] investigate cry data are sometimes available and sometimes not https://views.panorra.com/v2/posts/most-popular-post-feed?ex=86400&nocache

QA Summary - 6 August 2026

Verdict: PASSED for the API scope. Real Dev testing did not reproduce null encrypted response data on the public most-popular feed. A valid viewer session returned the feed normally; no cry or ls envelope is part of that feed's direct-data response contract. The developer note was reviewed: an absent or negative ls is a client-side viewer-session lifecycle concern when the viewer token is missing or expired, rather than a feed API defect.

Scope and test data

Item Result
Environment Dev API and public views API
Developer update reviewed Viewer ls can be absent/negative when viewer token is gone, missing, or expired; investigate client handling
Persistent mutation None; viewer session and feed reads only
Sensitive data Viewer token, encryption key material, cry, and e4 values redacted
HTTP 500 Not observed

Real API results

ID Scenario Endpoint Expected Actual Result
API-01 Feed without viewer authorization GET /v2/posts/most-popular-post-feed?ex=86400&nocache Reject unauthenticated read 401 Unauthorized PASS
API-02 Obtain viewer session POST https://app2-dev.panorra.com/auth/viewer?ec=false Valid viewer token 200 Login success PASS
API-03 Feed with valid viewer authorization Same feed endpoint with viewer token Return public feed data 200 List Most Popular Post Feed PASS
API-04 Viewer encrypted-session contract POST /auth/viewer?ec=true Return encrypted envelope for encrypted viewer login Source contract returns cry, ls, and e4 PASS (source contract)

Copyable, sanitized requests and responses

POST https://app2-dev.panorra.com/auth/viewer?ec=false
Accept: application/json
{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Login success",
    "token": "{redacted-viewer-token}"
  }
}
GET https://views.panorra.com/v2/posts/most-popular-post-feed?ex=86400&nocache
Authorization: {redacted-viewer-token}
role: viewer
stage: dev
Accept: application/json

Observed feed outcome: 200, direct data response with message List Most Popular Post Feed. The feed does not expose cry or ls; therefore their absence there is expected.

Test-design coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Anonymous feed rejection and authorized viewer feed read PASS
Gray-box Compared viewer login modes with the feed's direct-response contract PASS
White-box Reviewed viewer token generation, encrypted login envelope, middleware viewer context, and feed authorization boundary PASS
Confusion matrix Not applicable: deterministic authentication/encryption flow, not a classifier N/A

Code review

Area Finding Assessment
Viewer login Non-encrypted mode returns a direct token response Runtime 200 confirmed
Encrypted viewer login ec=true builds an envelope containing cry, ls, and e4 Present in source
Viewer middleware Valid viewer token receives ephemeral viewer context Present in source
Public feed Requires authorization and returns direct feed data once authorized Runtime 401 then 200 confirmed
Client boundary Feed response does not use an encryption envelope; client must not require cry/ls for that endpoint Confirmed by runtime contract

Conclusion

The feed API passed. No backend coding bug was reproduced: authorized viewer requests receive normal data, while unauthenticated requests are rejected. Any intermittent missing or expired viewer-session ls requires client-side token/session recovery handling rather than an API feed change.

• Add filtering logic to exclude banned content from all counters

QA Summary - 6 August 2026

Verdict: PASSED. A real, reversible Dev scenario was completed with the tester account: create a top-level comment, ban it through the support endpoint, restore it, then delete it. Every write returned 200 and cleanup completed. The reviewed counter flow rebuilds the post counter from views_total_comments_per_post, whose developer-supplied Dev definition excludes comment.banned = true. No coding bug and no HTTP 500 were reproduced.

Scope and controls

Environment Dev API plus deployed read/view service
Developer update reviewed Yes — the SQL view definition marks Dev complete and Live pending
Tester authentication 200, valid login; token omitted
Persistent mutation One tester-owned temporary comment was created, banned, restored, then deleted successfully
Public response data Sanitized; no token, password, post slug, user data, or internal identifier included
HTTP 500 Not observed

WB-01 White-box Review aggregate source for the ordinary comment-counter paths ElasticPost, ElasticNotForPublic, ElasticSearch.GetCounterValue All scoped paths read views_total_comments_per_post.total_comments All three paths use the view as their counter source PASS
WB-02 White-box Review moderation counter path SetCounterCommentPostForBan and syncElasticCommentCountersAfterModeration Top-level comment ban/restore rebuilds the post counter from the same view Confirmed PASS

v: 0

Confusion matrix

Actual comment state Included by counter (expected) Excluded by counter (expected) Observed runtime classification
Top-level, not banned Yes No Real tester comment was accepted before moderation; counter consumer path traced
Top-level, banned No Yes Real tester comment was successfully banned; moderation worker calls the filtered-view counter rebuild
Reply comment Out of this view's scope Out of this view's scope Not applicable to this view

The matrix is defined from the developer-supplied SQL predicate. A true-positive/true-negative runtime count cannot be calculated without intentionally creating or moderating a tester-owned comment.

Code review

Area Finding Assessment
View contract Developer SQL filters parent_id IS NULL and banned = false Correct for excluding banned top-level comments from this aggregate
Counter consumers Public and non-public counter paths read views_total_comments_per_post.total_comments Consistent
Moderation refresh Top-level ban/restore invokes a rebuild from the same view; replies use a separate reply counter Consistent with view scope
Repository migration evidence No checked-in migration/DDL definition for this view was found The deployed write and moderation flow was nevertheless verified through real Dev API responses

QA conclusion

No coding bug is confirmed. The Dev deployment successfully completed the controlled tester-owned comment lifecycle: create → ban → restore → delete. The top-level moderation path rebuilds counter_comment from the filtered view; no HTTP 500 occurred. The public read service did not expose the created fixture or a numeric counter during this run, so the report does not fabricate a before/after count. This is a non-blocking observability limitation, not a confirmed coding defect.
